title: Tahir Hussain Convicted of Abetting Rioting in 2020 Delhi Riots Case
excerpt: The Karkardooma court acquitted 12 co-accused of all charges; sentencing arguments for the former AAP councillor are set for November 16.
body:
• A Delhi court on Saturday convicted former Aam Aadmi Party councillor Tahir Hussain of abetment to rioting in a case linked to the 2020 northeast Delhi riots, while acquitting him of all other charges.
  • The court acquitted all 12 of his co-accused of all charges. Arguments on the quantum of sentence against Hussain are listed for November 16.
  • This is Hussain's second conviction in the riots cases: he was sentenced to life imprisonment earlier for the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma.

A Delhi court on Saturday convicted former Aam Aadmi Party councillor Tahir Hussain for the offence of abetment to rioting in a case linked to the 2020 northeast Delhi riots. Additional Sessions Judge Praveen Singh of the Karkardooma Courts convicted Hussain under Section 147 of the Indian Penal Code, read with Section 109 on abetment, while acquitting him of the remaining charges.

The court also acquitted the 12 other accused in the case — among them Mohammad Shadab, Shah Alam, Riyasat Ali, Gulfam, Mohammad Rihan, Arshad Qayyum, and Irshad Ahmed — of all charges. The judge listed November 16 for hearing arguments on the quantum of sentence against Hussain. A detailed order is awaited.

Context & Background

The case arose from FIR No. 120 of 2020 registered at the Dayalpur police station, covering offences under IPC Sections 147, 148, 149 (rioting), 427 (mischief and damage to property), 436 (mischief by fire), and 120B (criminal conspiracy).

https://x.com/iAtulKrishan1/status/2108894988398715003

The complaint was filed by Irshad Ali, who said the shop where he worked was looted and set on fire on February 24, 2020. He alleged losses of around Rs 17 to 18 lakh from articles robbed from the shop and about Rs 10 lakh from damage to the building. A second complainant, Mohd. Zahid, stated that the rioters were raising slogans in Hussain's name. During the investigation, two constables identified Hussain as he was a public figure they already knew. He was formally arrested on April 21, 2020, in Mandoli Jail while already in judicial custody in another riots case.

Impact & Analysis

This is the second conviction of Tahir Hussain in the 2020 riots prosecutions. Earlier, the same judge convicted him — along with four other men — for the murder of Intelligence Bureau staffer Ankit Sharma during the riots, in FIR 65 of 2020, also at Dayalpur police station. Sharma had left home in the evening to buy groceries and never returned; his body was later found in a drain near Chand Bagh Pulia with dozens of sharp injuries.

In that case, Hussain was sentenced to life imprisonment. The Delhi Police had sought the death penalty, but the court declined, noting there was no record of violent disposition or prior criminal involvement on the convicts' part. The contrast between the two outcomes — life imprisonment for the murder case, acquittals for 12 co-accused here — underscores how differently the evidence has landed across the cluster of riots cases.

What's Next

The court will hear arguments on the sentence for the abetment-to-rioting conviction on November 16. The detailed judgment has not yet been released. Hussain remains in custody, already serving a life sentence in the Ankit Sharma murder case, and his bail plea was rejected by the Delhi High Court last year. Further appeals in both cases are expected.
